name: bug-fix
invariants: No write-capable node is reachable before the current brief is approved: user_explicitly_approved, or auto_approved_by_policy when the user setting HM_APPROVAL or HM_APPROVAL_REPOS resolves to auto and the brief has no open questions. Auto approval also needs every acceptance_map criterion covered or out of scope with a reason.
A bug fix is not complete without reproduction or explicit equivalent verification evidence.
triage goes straight to brief only when an investigation report from the investigate workflow is provided; that report's reproduction or equivalent evidence stands in for reproduce.
A blocking finding cannot transition directly to done.
Every repair is followed by required checks and re-review.
publish commits, pushes, and opens a PR only as .ai-harness/harness.json git_policy allows; it never merges, force-pushes, or pushes to the base branch.

Work that was pushed is not done until remote CI for the pushed commit has finished green or the repository has no remote CI; local runs of the CI commands do not stand in for it, a failure goes back through repair, and remote CI that cannot be observed ends as unverified, never as done. When the run pushes and the repository has CI configuration, remote CI is the final gate: the driver does not run the brief's final_checks locally (nor in sync_base); local final_checks run only in repositories without remote CI.

Only the merge node merges, and only when the user's personal delivery level (HM_DELIVERY_LEVEL) is merge or deploy and the run is not unattended: the driver reads the pull request and the base branch protection from its host and merges with the head pinned to the pushed, reviewed commit after remote CI passed, only into a branch the host protects with required approvals and only when every merge condition (the user's HM_MERGE_* raised to the host's required approvals and checks) holds; an unmet condition waits (resume checks again); a merge blocked only by a conflict with the base goes to sync_base, and any other blocked one goes to user_decision, never bypassed.

sync_base brings the latest origin base into the work branch only with a normal merge and a normal push (a fast-forward of the branch), never a rebase, a force push, or a push to the base branch; an agent session only resolves conflicts and never commits or pushes; the driver pushes only after the run's checks pass again, then goes back through remote_ci and merge; it also takes in a single base merge commit pushed from outside during remote_ci, and any other move is still an invariant violation; reaching limits.max_base_syncs, an unresolved conflict, or a failing check goes to user_decision.

Merged work is not done until every post-merge check the delivery level covers passed for the merge commit (target_ci, then deploy_check_cmd, then smoke_cmd); a failure or a result that cannot be observed ends at user_decision with rollback instructions, never as done, and the driver never reverts on its own. The one exception is target_ci under the user's HM_TARGET_CI=notify (or HM_TARGET_CI_REPOS): it reads the merge commit CI once without waiting; failed or unverified still goes to user_decision, and a still-running CI is tracked by a detached watcher that records the result and alerts on a failure (progress.log ALERT, state alerts, desktop notification) while the run continues; the driver still never reverts.

A change with ui_scenarios is not done until ui_review has rendered and operated them in the render target .ai-harness/docs/ui.md declares for each screen (chromium when it declares none; a simulator or emulator for native screens), never another engine in its place, with no blocking UI finding; ui_review follows the project ui-review contract, does not change the working tree, and a UI that could not be verified ends at user_decision as unverified, never as done.
